A Message's own record beside it (Mikhail, 2026-09-15: "двигайтесь к"
this form; "Все остальное -- не Message и должно в итоге перевестись на LMX
то есть стать внутренностью Message"; the handoff flag confirmed by him the
same day):

    typedef struct LmxMsg {
        volatile uint_fast8_t running;       /* 1 at launch; polled while root executes; 0 is the
                                                parent's stop request, and is set at exit */
        volatile uint_fast8_t success;       /* 0 at launch; 1 is written by user code */
        volatile uint_fast8_t handoff_safe;  /* 1 is written by the Message itself when it has left
                                                its last turn and nothing native uses its arena:
                                                the arena may be attached (19.29.7, 19.29.8) */
        Lmx *root;                           /* the root of its graph; its arena is reached from it */
        unsigned index;                      /* its index at its parent: the whole of what the
                                                hierarchical address a.b.c.d... adds at this level;
                                                the full address is composed by walking the parent
                                                links, and a letter carries the destination address
                                                in full (Mikhail, 2026-09-16: the address arrays are
                                                optimized to the index at the parent); the address
                                                changes with the parent at a parent change;
                                                delivery is hop by hop through parents' inboxes, every
                                                L3 Thread a postman for one step deciding by address
                                                (Mikhail, 2026-09-16, verbatim in 19.29.7) */
    } LmxMsg;

Mikhail, 2026-09-15, verbatim, on the two flags: "success && !running, с выходом выставляется running = 0. Просто running опрашивается при выполнении Lmx* root и я же не знаю как кокнретный планировщик устроен и когда выйдет. Но условия выхода очевидно есть!" (one that
ended by success is success and not running; at exit running = 0 is set; running is
simply polled while Lmx* root executes, and how a particular scheduler is
arranged and when it exits is not fixed here, but the exit conditions
obviously exist).

Everything else is not Message and is, in the end, written in LMX as the
inside of a Message (its Structure data in its own arena): an L3 Thread's
record adds its mailbox (the one synchronized collection of Messages) and
its scheduler and maintenance state as such data.
Mikhail, 2026-09-15, verbatim, on that inside: "и транслируется в LMX как внутренность Message." -- то есть записывается в "struct Lmx *root; " , и на L1 нужно сделать имитацию (то есть не имитацию а код вкоторый L2 и L3 будут разворачиваться) and, correcting
himself the same minute: "то есть записывается в "struct Lmx *root;"" это уже на L2 там лежит код который с этими Message и работает. А на L1 просто тот код который _будет порождаться_. (that inside is written into what
`root` reaches; on L2 that is where the code working with these Messages
lies; on L1 there is simply the code that will be generated). And on the
shape of that code: "В точности как имитируется L2 на Си -- функция с аргументами ,скрытми ргументами и узлом графа." (exactly as L2 is imitated in C: a function
with arguments, hidden arguments and the graph node). Hence, verbatim:
"Поэтому структура Message как данные остается и на Си -- в точности как стуктура Lmx" (therefore the Message structure as data stays in C as well,
exactly like the Lmx structure): the record above is a C data type beside
Lmx, not something later rewritten in LMX. And on a sentence of the
coordinator's that stood here, "the C keeps only the native primitives (the
thread, the mailbox's monitor)", verbatim: "the C keeps only the native primitives (the thread, the mailbox's monitor)»" -- это для L3 Thread? Он тоже пишется на L1,переноситс на L2 и остаток на L3. Разумеется на L2 остается низкий уровень, а причем тут вообще Си? Ты же не пишешьв Си на ассемблере встаквки "потому что надо компилировать". Удаляй (is that about the L3
Thread? it too is written in L1, moved to L2 and the remainder to L3; of
course the low level stays on L2, but what has C to do with it; you do not
write assembler insertions in C "because it has to compile"; delete it).
And, the same day, on the whole of the synchronization, verbatim: "синхронизации только по inbox outbox более чем достаточно, многократно проговоренная мной схема по которой ребенок  иродитель взаимно опрашиваются (в приоритете ребенок опрашивает -- он и должен оставлять след что живой) тоже совершенна надежна, никаких утечек там никогда не будет так как от пользовательского L3 однопоточного кода это не зависит. L2 и L1 это уже ответственность юзера, но мы можем писать без этого"
(synchronization only on inbox and outbox is more than enough; the scheme
he has stated many times, the child and the parent polling each other
mutually, with the child's poll the priority since it is the child that
must leave the trace that it is alive, is perfectly reliable too; there
will never be leaks there, since it does not depend on the user's
single-threaded L3 code; L2 and L1 are the user's responsibility, but we
can write without that). And on why nothing can hang, verbatim: "если у тебя у каждого родителя стоит таймаут на ребенка и у ребенка на родителя таймаут и в каждой буквально точке (цикл, вход, выход) проверяетс running, у одной арены строго один поток, то у тебя зависание никогда не будет дольше чем таймаут, это схема железобетонная. Программа может упасть, но завсинуть -- с чего, на чем? На ресурсах или что-то в этом роде? В Си есть механизм прибить поток принудительно (потом реализуем, сейчас бы хоть ядро запустить) , в конце концов по таймауту сработает корневой поток и тупо выйдет из процесс ОС. Тут не может быть никаких зависаний"
(if every parent has a timeout on its child and every child a timeout on
its parent, and at literally every point, loop, entry, exit, running is
checked, and one arena has strictly one thread, then no hang ever lasts
longer than the timeout; the scheme is reinforced concrete; a program
can crash, but hang on what, resources or the like? C has a way to kill
a thread by force, to be done later, now the kernel has to run at all;
in the end the root thread's timeout fires and simply leaves the OS
process; there can be no hangs here). And on deadlock, verbatim: "deadlock никогда не случится если синхронизация только внутри очереди сообщений на чтение-запись письма в минималистическом java-стиле. Там вообще нечему зависать"
(a deadlock never happens if synchronization is only inside the message
queue, on reading and writing a letter, in the minimalist Java style;
there is nothing there to hang on).
And on what L1 is for, verbatim: "Вы пытаетесь писать на Си, а на Си (L1) надо просто пилить ядро _на котором_ уже пилить дальнейший функционал самого ядра. Это как я бы попросил на goto имитировать все циклы, а вы бы заменили задание на "написать примеры while и for"  -- совершенно разне задачи" (you are trying to write in
C, while in C, that is L1, one simply builds the kernel on which the further
functionality of the kernel itself is then built; as if I asked you to
imitate all loops with goto and you replaced the task with "write examples
of while and for": entirely different tasks). And, the same day, on what
the whole is, verbatim: "Это полноценный ООП язык, объект --Message, исполняемый  объект -- L3 Thread. Такие же странные вопросы ты можешь задавать любому языку программирования высокого уровня.Потому он и называется "L3 Thread"" (this is a full object-oriented
language: the object is Message, the executing object is L3 Thread; the
same strange questions could be asked of any high-level language; that is
why it is called "L3 Thread").

The arena and its table (Mikhail, 2026-09-17). An arena provides N arrays and one
table address -> descriptor of the contents, for typing `void *`, and it may attach
another arena; that is the whole mechanism and nothing else is needed (verbatim: "У
нас есть арена (там менеджер) она предоставляет N массивов и таблицу
адрес->дескриптор содержимого для типизации void *, также может присоединять другую
арену. ЧТО ЕЩЁ НАДО?"). The arrays never move, so it is the table ENTRIES that are
ordered and bisected, never the arrays (verbatim: "У тебя есть N массивов в арене.
Как ты можешь его отсортировать если у каждого массива адрес фиксирован?!!!! Ты
должен сделать _таблицу адрес->дескриптор массива_ и после вставку в таблицу делает
менеджер арены (в том числе когда он присоединяет другую арену)"). Lookups are
bisection, not a walk of the table (verbatim: "надеюсь не простым перебором а
нормальным бинарным"). Only the arena's manager inserts, and it inserts for each array
that joins the arena, including when the arena attaches another one; attaching appends
arrays, moves no address, and leaves the existing entries exactly where they are.

For every Array type the arena keeps its own array of descriptors - length and a typed
pointer to the data (verbatim: "ДЛЯ КАЖДОГО ТИП МАССИВА АРЕНА ЗАВОДИТ СВОЙ МАССИВ
ДЕСКРИПТОРОВ (длиина и типизированный указатель на дату) И ПОЕХАЛИ"). A descriptor
carries no type field: its type follows from which descriptor array the descriptor
itself lies in, not from anything the descriptor holds. Typing lies exclusively in the
address range, and as many ranges (types) as needed may be created; a primitive is
laid down directly, a composite type lays down its descriptor, and that is all
(verbatim: "то есть типизация лежит исключительно в диапазоне адресов и вы можете этих
диапазонов (типов) заводить сколько вам угодно. Примитивы ложить прямо, для составных
типов класть их дескрипторы -- ВСЁ"). Arrays are not a special case
of anything (verbatim: "ЧЕМ МАССИВЫ ОТЛИЧАЮТСЯ ОТ ВСЕГО ОСТАЛЬНОГО? НИЧЕМ!!!"): a
Structure's child-pointer array is an array of the arena like every other and is in the
table like every other. What a slot address does not do is type the child stored in it
- that is the child's VALUE, and it is classified on its own by the table above.

Nothing gates writing into a cell. Code that holds a reference, having determined its
type once, casts the pointer and writes STRAIGHT into the cell, because a cell's
address never changes; this is obligatory (verbatim: "_Получив дескриптор типа код
сразу делает приведение типа указателя и пишет напрямую в ячейку_ _Это обязательно_";
"Код как раз обладая ссылкой и определив один раз ее тип _может писать прямо в массив
так как адрес ячейки не меняется_"). The table is consulted only where the type is NOT
known - an untyped `void *` arriving from elsewhere; where the type is known
statically, no lookup happens at all. There is no per-owner inventory of ranges and no
other side list: the arrays, their descriptors and the table are the whole of it.

Eternal branches are a different mechanism (verbatim: "«вечная ветка» это совершенно
другой механизм"). Inside an eternal branch every `void * data` points into the root
Message's arena - not the whole of it, its immutable part (verbatim: "В вечной ветке
всё void * data по идее должно было указывать на арену корневого Message, причем не на
всю а на ее неизменяемую часть"). Eternal branches and eternal values have addresses
like everything else, so the translator substitutes their direct values and explicit
types into the code, as `const`, a thousand times over, and nothing more is needed
there (verbatim: "Но у вечных веток и вечных значений так же самое есть адреса.
_ЗНАЧИТ ТРАНСЛЯТОР ЛЕГКО ПОДСТАВЛЯЕТ В КОД ПРЯМЫЕ ЗНАЧЕНИЯ И ЯВНЫЕ ТИПЫ ЕЩЕ и ДЕЛАЯ
ИХ ТЫСЯЧУ РАЗ CONST_ -- РАЗВЕ НЕ ТАК? ТАМ ЖЕ ВООБЩЕ НИЧЕГО БОЛЬШЕ НЕ НУЖНО"). A
reference from a mutable field to an eternal branch is an ordinary reference to that
branch's descriptor in its own arena (verbatim: "Ссылка же в изменяемом поле на вечную
ветку это обычная ссылка на дескриптор ветки в собственной арене -- разве не так?").
No eternal-range list and no other side table exists as a mechanism.

For every Array type T the arena keeps its own array of descriptors - length and a
typed pointer to the data - and a descriptor's type follows from which descriptor
array the descriptor itself lies in, never from a field it holds. The arena provides
N arrays and one table address -> descriptor of the contents, for typing `void *`;
the arrays never move, so the table's ENTRIES are what is ordered and bisected, and
only the arena's manager inserts into it, including when the arena attaches another
arena (2, Mikhail, 2026-09-17, verbatim there). No per-owner inventory of ranges and
no eternal-range list is part of the mechanism; an eternal branch is a different
mechanism, settled in 2.

Clarification (2026-09-14, Mikhail). An L3 Thread is a Message: a Message is
simply an isolated LMX graph, and an L3 Thread is a Message that can attach
and/or execute any Message. Every L3 Thread is a Message; not every Message is
an L3 Thread (a template and a letter have no turn; a launched child does).
The mailbox and the provision for a turn exist only at an L3 Thread, even when
it is executed from outside and no thread of its own is started. An L3 Thread
launches Messages; being launched is not an obligatory property of a Message.
The scheduler exists only in varieties of L3 Thread: it allocates execution to
the Messages that L3 Thread attached (a consumer schedules the Messages it
attached) and removes on timeout as judged by the children's own checks; it
does not manage running children in full: in normal operation children close
themselves and schedule their own children the same way. Polling has one
direction, child to parent (19.29.7.1); a child closes itself after prolonged
absence of its parent, and closing from above is the second, emergency
mechanism.

Clarification (2026-09-14, Mikhail): one arena, one lane, one writer. A
Message's scheduler and management state is written only on that Message's
own lane; no other thread writes into a Message's data, and this holds for
the C runtime exactly as for L2, because it is not a property of the graph
system but of the Message. A parent therefore
keeps no list that another thread appends to: a child pushing itself into
its parent's ready list from the child's thread, and a UI thread writing
into many parents' lists, are implementation errors of the L1 prototype and
are removed from it, not carried into L2. A request to another lane (mapping
a child onto the UI lane) is a Message to that lane's mailbox; the mailbox's
admission lock is the one cross-lane synchronization the model permits
(19.29.6).
Ownership of cells, for the rule "written only on the owner's lane"
(2026-09-14): (1) a Message owns its arena, its scheduler record and cursor,
its mailbox except admission, its native
users and handoff-safe marks, its success, and its own running clear at
end_turn; its lane is whichever thread holds its turn, so a host-driven turn
is that Message's lane. (2) The parent owns the supervision cells about its
direct children wherever they sit physically: committed, tracked, the
last-heard time, the execution mapping written at bind (so the authority to
bind, rebind or unbind a Message is its parent's lane, or the host outside
any turn while the bootstrap is the host; a Message does not map or unmap
itself and a sibling's turn does not; the settling lane's unbind at release
is the parent's write, or the host's for an orphan; clarified 2026-09-14), the family chain
(first and last child, siblings' links, the parent link at link, unlink and
supervision handoff), and the settle writes (the storage moved into the
parent, the child's graph and init at settle). (3) Control flags are single
cells with one designated cross-lane writer, by the flags' philosophy: the
parent writes a child's running=0 and closing (stop).
What is removed by this rule: a parent's ready lists and context lists
appended by a child's, a sender's or a UI thread's lane; a child unlinking
itself from its parent's list; the parent's step reads its children's own
cells instead.
Mikhail, 2026-09-15, on the child's readiness flag this paragraph used to
name (written by the sender at admission, read by the parent's step),
verbatim: "готовность ребёнка его собственным" --готовность к чему?! Удаляй (readiness for what? delete it): the flag and its
sentences are removed above; a Message's mail is what its own loop finds in
its mailbox. The same day, on a delivery history the L1 runtime kept
(the last ids per sender, dropping repeats), verbatim: "ящик помнил последние id от каждого отправителя и отбрасывал повторы («не более одного раза»)." -- какая-то выдумка. Удаляй все. (some
invention; delete it all): no such mechanism in the core.

Clarification (2026-09-15, Mikhail, verbatim): "Там не должно быть общих
блокировок. У очереди писем только своя внутренняя блокировка коллекции,
всё" (there must be no shared locks; the mail queue has only its own internal
collection lock, that is all); "блокировка только локальная у коллекции
сообщений может быть, больше блокировокне требуется даже локальных -- их в
проекте не длолжно быть больше вообще" (the only lock there may be is the
local lock of the message collection; no other locks are needed, not even
local ones; there must be none of them in the project at all); "значит
реализуйте полноценную арену для каждого MEssage, как описано в спеке. Без
этого Message не имеет смысла" (so implement a full arena for each Message,
as described in the spec (19.29.2); without it a Message makes no sense).
Deleted the same day by his order: the former item (5) of the ownership list
above (runtime-level structures kept under the executor's lock), written
2026-09-14 by the review chat as its own consequence, never his words.
Clarification (2026-09-15, Mikhail). On closing a parent whose children have no
thread of their own, verbatim: "Закрытие родителя это авария. Каждый ребенок
закрывает себя сам и для его детей это такая же авария. Если дети L3 Thread
но реализация такая что у них нет своего потока, а они последовательно
выполняются, то это нюансы реализации. Разумеется в этом случае закрытие
родителя затягивается так как планировщик должен пройтись и выполнить чужую
работу -- но зачем вам вообще сейчас такие потоки если вы не можете даже ядро
архитектуры запилить точно по спеке?" (closing a parent is an emergency; each
child closes itself, and for its children it is the same emergency; children
that are L3 Threads without a thread of their own, run sequentially, are an
implementation nuance that drags the parent's close out with others' work; but
why have such threads at all now, when the core is not yet built exactly by the
spec?). The reading that "for now every L3 Thread runs on its own OS thread, and the
sequential mapping is removed from the runtime" is withdrawn -- Mikhail,
2026-09-17, verbatim: "я такого не говорил, это модели издеваются. Я сказал
что lmx_thread имеет API и реализации могут быть разными. В том числе
бегающая и небегающая." So the object carries an API and its implementation
is open by design: an OS thread of its own and being stepped by its parent
are both admissible, and nothing here requires either one. This agrees with
11541, 11548-11549 and 12649 above ("no dedicated OS thread per Message is
required") and with 19.29.6's own definition of a running Message as a
logical serial execution lane.
Confirmed by Mikhail the same day ("да") in this wording, on the runtime-level
structures the L1 implementation kept under its executor's lock: there is no
root list (the root is one, R0, and its children are an ordinary child list in
R0's arena); there is no walk at deletion (the close is R0's own closing
end-turn); the slot list served only the L1 delete loop and its address lookup
and goes without replacement; the retire queue goes (a closed child's storage
is its parent's settle write); a lane's own queue is that Message's mailbox.
Mikhail, 2026-09-15, verbatim: "Синхронизация только локальная в почтовом
ящике каждого L3 Thread -- больше в проекте нет (за исключением поддержки
ресивера \"synchronized\")" (synchronization is only local, in the mailbox
of each L3 Thread; there is none else in the project, except the support of
the receiver "synchronized", 20.5.7).
Mikhail, 2026-09-15, verbatim, on the UI lane (until then a Message without a
thread of its own, stepped by the root's turn, which he called a crooked
implementation): "Полоса на экране не может не быть L3 Thread. Message без L3 Thread это просто письмо. Полоса же это полноценный объект. Объектов у нас не так много как в SmallTalk но все равно много. Поэтому реализация L3 Thread планировщика который не запускает потоки детей а бегает по ним сам -- ближайшая задача для myxa_manager" (a lane on the screen cannot fail to be an
L3 Thread; a Message without an L3 Thread is just a letter; a lane is a full
object; we do not have as many objects as Smalltalk, but still many; so the
implementation of an L3 Thread scheduler that does not launch its children's
threads but runs over them itself is the nearest task for mixa_manager).
Mikhail, 2026-09-15, verbatim, on the host's Win32 message loop (the
coordinator had called its blocking GetMessage a property of Win32 outside
the model): "ну так для того и существует отличие ядра Message, которое полностью подн контролем языка, от платформенных реализаций L3 Thread! Просто положите Win32 GetMessage в потомка L3 Thread (потомки у нас создаются merge) и все, в чем проблема? Будет заполнять inbox который свой поток будет читать." (that is what the difference between the Message
kernel, wholly under the language's control, and the platform
implementations of L3 Thread is for: put Win32 GetMessage into a descendant
L3 Thread, descendants being created by merge, and that is all; it fills an
inbox that its own thread reads).
Mikhail, 2026-09-15, verbatim, on the mailbox's synchronization: "тупейший вложенный synchronized по локу на чтение и запись как в Java, без остальных усложнений вообще. "notify получает не «поток», а поток-владелец ящика" -- ну а смысл его нотифицировать если он занят в turn?!!! Выйдет и посмотрит" (the
dumbest nested synchronized on the lock for reading and writing, as in Java,
with no other complications at all; what is the point of notifying the owner
thread if it is busy in a turn? it comes out and looks). And on the owner
thread when its mailbox is empty after a turn: ""завершается ли поток владельца при пустом ящике после выхода из turn'а" -- нет!!!! L3 Thread точно так же завершается только по success пользовательским кодом. Каким образом вы будете код писать иначе?" (no; an L3 Thread ends
only by success set by user code, like everything else; how else would you
write code?). And: "никакого success у многих фоновых задач вообще нет, то есть это не может быть правилом ядра \"в ящике ничего нет поэтому ухожу\"" (many background tasks have no success at all, so "nothing in the mailbox, therefore I leave" cannot be a rule of the core). And, confirming that the owner thread's loop
runs on between turns and looks into its mailbox each time round: "иначе не
реализуешь цикл бесконечный -- он тупо не будет проверять почту!!!"
(otherwise you cannot implement the infinite loop; it simply will not check
the mail).
And on the coordinator's words "the thread with its infinite loop", the same
day, verbatim: "поток с бесконечным циклом" -- цикл в L3 Thread очеивдно прерывается по success==1 (the loop in an L3 Thread obviously
breaks on success==1). And, the same hour, verbatim: "success && !running, с выходом выставляется running = 0. Просто running опрашивается при выполнении Lmx* root и я же не знаю как кокнретный планировщик устроен и когда выйдет. Но условия выхода очевидно есть!": the
exit conditions exist: by the model no turn of root repeats once success ==
1, since success belongs to Lmx* root, the main functionality; what the L3
Thread's scheduler does with its children after that is implementation, as
children may run on the same thread, and so is where the return stands

Release of a Message and its family (clarification 2026-09-14, Mikhail). A
released branch is never retained: releasing a Message releases its whole
subtree, and release does not wait for the children to finish. Every close
and free behaviour follows from three rules. (1) A parent that forcibly
releases a child starts a chain reaction: the child closes and releases its
own direct children the same way (each Message services its own direct
children, 19.28.R2.2), and the branch's slots and arenas are freed by that
chain, never at process end. (2) A child's own orderly close after sustained
absence of its parent starts the same chain for its subtree. (3) The runtime
never sets success on a parent whose children are still running=1 with
success=0; when the parent's own algorithm sets success in that state it
thereby declares the children's work unneeded, and the same chain closes and
releases them. The endpoint step of an orderly close (the parent may first
take a stopped child's final state or storage; model sections 32 and 34) is
a step inside the chain, not a reason to keep a closed branch's slots.
(4) There is no release of a child "into the open": the only way a running
Message (running=1) survives the closing of its parent is a handoff of
supervision to another LIVE parent, chosen by the closing parent among the
Messages whose capability it holds, and not necessarily the closing parent's
own parent (corrected 2026-09-14, Mikhail). Supervision handoff moves the
child's parent capability and its place in a scheduler; the child keeps its
own arena, mailbox and turn. It is distinct from storage adoption, which
still requires a non-executing, handoff-safe source (19.29.7). A child not
handed over closes with the chain. For the root Message the only possible
new parent is the virtual ancestor, the World Wide Mix placement (19.28.10)
at the level of the OS process, so a handoff from the root means "launch an
OS process"; that target is a refusing stub with its own status until World
Wide Mix (19.28.10) and the transport of section 35 are implemented, since
the tree above the root exists algorithmically and is not implemented
(Mikhail, 2026-09-14: the stub stays until World Wide Mix is implemented);
stage 5, which makes OS startup the root Message, fixes only the call site
and the ancestor's address.
(5) Adoption closes the adopted (Mikhail, 2026-09-14): the storage transfer
of an arena adoption closes the adopted Message; it does not remain a live
Message beside its transferred storage. Whatever the adopter then spawns from
the adopted content is a child of the adopter, the Message that processed it,
not of the adopted one. The fork is strict, and it is the L3 Thread / Message
distinction of 19.28.R2.2: a Message either works itself, which makes it an
L3 Thread (its own turn and its own place under the Message that launched
it), or is worked on by others, which is what a plain Message is (attached,
adopted, closed by the L3 Thread that processes it); the two have a different
genesis and therefore a different place in the hierarchy. Supervision
handoff (rule 4) moves a live Message; adoption moves storage and ends the
Message. Hence exactly two ways keep a line of descendants beyond the closing
of their parent (Mikhail, 2026-09-14): (i) spawn a plain Message and send it,
so that whatever it spawns at the receiver is the receiver's line; (ii) spawn
an L3 Thread and hand its supervision to another branch. A subtree that is
neither closes with the chain.
Three consequences of rules (1)-(3) for the runtime, read together with
19.29.8, which selects the settling policy (review chat, 2026-09-14; corrected
the same day against 19.29.8): (i) the parent's dispose of a settled failed
child settles it as 19.29.8 says: the runtime transfers the child's logical
arena to the parent without copying and retains the failed root there, then
releases the child's slot; the parent neither drops a failed arena nor has to
call the adoption itself, and a dispose of a failed child with storage is not
refused; a successful child's history is reclaimed by default; (ii) release
does not wait for the children to be disposed one by one: a parent's dispose
or adopt of a child settles that child's whole settled subtree by the chain,
bottom-up as 19.29.8 describes (G's arena joins C, then C's joins P), and the
guards that remain are that the child is not running, is handoff-safe and has
no native users; (iii) a descendant still running at release time is closed
by the chain (its closing flag set, as by any stop) and becomes an orphan: a
successful orphan is settled at its end-turn and reclaimed, arena and slot,
by the settling lane at the root's next maintenance point (the host's drive
today, the root's between-turns maintenance from stage 5 (c) on), the same
on the host path and the mapped path (clarified 2026-09-14: one reclaim
site, never retained, never adopted); a failed orphan
keeps its handoff-safe arena under the separate parent-loss/orphan-retention
timeout of 19.29.8 and self-reclaims when it expires (an orphan is settled
only by that policy, never by its supervising root's ordinary settle step:
once orphans are the root Message's children, stage 5 (d), the parent's
settle chain skips a child marked orphan; clarified 2026-09-14); the parent's release
returns at once, and the branch is drained, not retained, while those turns
and timeouts run. An orphan is re-rooted at the runtime for its drain (a
top-level Message with no parent, reachable like any root, closing by the
chain); stage 5, which makes OS startup the root Message, makes it that root
Message's child. The children of a stopped Message (clarified 2026-09-14): a
stopped Message has no lane, so nothing runs its children's turns from it;
its stop requests their close; a child whose inbox is empty is closed by the
maintenance without a turn, and a child on its own context runs its closing
turn there; a child with pending input under a host-mapped stopped parent
waits until the parent is disposed, when the chain re-roots it under the
root Message, whose step runs its closing turn like any child's; nothing
else steps it (no ancestor rule, no maintenance step, no authority of a
stopped Message). An unbound closing Message has no handler and no lane, so
its close is end-turn bookkeeping written by the maintaining lane (the
host's drive today, the root's maintenance later), not a step, and it
leaves the Message stopped and handoff-safe so that its parent's dispose or
adopt can settle it; a Message that nothing could ever settle would be the
retention rule (1) forbids (clarified 2026-09-14). The orphan-retention timeout is a runtime policy value with
a default, settable per runtime like the liveness deadlines. A settled
Message (not running, handoff-safe) has no lane; the lane that settles it
writes its cells (the endpoint step), which is how the chain's writes fit
the one-lane rule of 19.28.R2.2.

verbatim): "running=0 is set, and at the end of its turn the closing Message
does the same to its children; that is all"; "the executor frees its own
memory"; "each of our L3 Threads has its own scheduler and garbage
collector".

9.1.4 and 1.7 for the lead's stage-5 design; none of them needed a new

creates the root Message R0 (address 1, the only Message without a parent
capability), and a rootless runtime "for embedding" does not exist, since an
embedder is outside LMX and reaches the runtime only through R0's mailbox
admission; (ii) the process entry (1.7) runs inside R0's own turns: the first
execution thread's Message is R0, its initial Message carries the settings
and the user input supplied at entry, and the entry program is R0's handler,
not a child spawned for it (9.1.4: the translator does not implicitly spawn
further Messages); (iii) nothing remains of a "host" outside any turn: every
authority the L1 bootstrap gave the host (ingress, drive, the UI lane's step,
the parent's step over top-level Messages, the logical clock, teardown)
belongs to R0's turn loop, and the historical host ingress V0 is not
normative; (iv) there is one top level: Messages created without a parent
become R0's children, orphans are re-rooted under R0 keeping their retention
policy (19.29.8: R0 is the lane that assigns a failed orphan's deadline and
reclaims it; nobody adopts an orphan's arena), and the UI lane of 19.28.R2.2
is R0's child mapped to R0's lane, the main thread; (v) the supervision
handoff from R0 to the virtual World Wide Mix ancestor stays a refusing stub
with its own status until 19.28.10 and the transport of section 35 are
implemented; stage 5 fixes only the call site and the ancestor's address.

Clarification (2026-09-14, Mikhail). Completion sets success=1 only;
running=0 follows success=1 only at the turn boundary, in end_turn. Inside a
turn running stays 1, so running=0 observed inside a turn is a stop request,
never the Message's own completion. The running flag is written by whoever
executed the Message: a Message executed on its own turn clears it at its
end_turn; a Message consumed by attachment (an ordinary letter) is executed by
the consumer's thread and mailbox, and the consumer clears it at the boundary
of its own turn. In transit a letter therefore stays running=1, success=0;
running=0 with success=0 at a boundary is the failed outcome that the parent
settles through the handoff boundary below. The sentence "it sets success=1
and then running=0" in the closing paragraph below is read with this order:
the two writes are separated by the turn boundary.

This is settled, not open. Mikhail, 2026-09-17, verbatim, on being asked whether
the capability should be struck: "оставляем synchronized как общую возможность
языка L2 -- уже много раз говорил. КАК ТЫ БУДЕШЬ ПЕРЕПИСЫВАТЬ НА L2 БЕЗ
SYNCHRONIZED?!!!" The project's "no locks" rule governs the KERNEL's own
implementation -- the only lock the design takes there is a mailbox's admission --
and never removes the language's ability to express synchronization. A language
without it could not be used to rewrite the very mechanisms that need it.

Its scope, Mikhail, 2026-09-17, verbatim: "Никаких локов за пределами почтового
ящика. Локов вообще как сущности нет только в L3 по спеке."
